error.name: TransportUnavailableError
error.message: DeRPC: anonymous transport is closed; refusing to send (no direct fallback)

limits: Same-party test wrappers and gateway, public-node upstreams and mock ENS identities: no public ENS registration or independent-operator claim.
Both onions are disposable and removed after this check; the private keys never leave container tmpfs.
Controlled unavailability is an actual HTTP503 returned by a test-only /rpc ingress gate; the actual wrapper identity and beacon routes remain available.
Initial selection is explicitly limited to one operator; this functional check is not evidence of global ranking or random-selection fairness.

Sequential public-fixture warmups verify node-a and node-b individually before the group/outage stages; these are reported separately. The additional operator is explicitly selected only for the later cross-operator stage.
No production timeouts, proof verification, isolation policy or existing service are changed.

This check does not exercise finalized operator-directory discovery, rotation, delisting or permission changes. Optional generic ENS resolution is a separate result and cannot convert a failed operator test into a pass.

evidenceScope.gatewayOwnership: Existing same-party local WebRTC gateway; endpoint and certificate are omitted from this artifact.
evidenceScope.identity: multi.derpc.eth and mevblocker.derpc.eth are explicit mock labels, not demonstrated public ENS registrations. The two onion wrappers share one configured mock signer.
evidenceScope.upstreams: Both local wrappers proxy the same public execution and beacon upstreams. The later explicit MEVBlocker fallback reaches the same execution service through a Tor exit.
evidenceScope.networkObservation: Host transport dispatches plus Firefox page request events; not an operating-system packet capture or an anonymity proof. No external browser HTTP request was observed. Current source includes same-origin content-addressed worker acquisition hints.
evidenceScope.controlledFailure: HTTP503 at a test-only ingress gate for /rpc; beacon and identity remained live. This models endpoint RPC unavailability, not destruction of the onion service.
evidenceScope.resourceCleanup: The runner closed its browser, both wrapper processes and ingress gates, and removed the owned Tor container and tmpfs onion keys. Its separate isolated Vite server was stopped after the run; original project services were preserved.

earlierAttempts.cause: Worker startup failed before any execution or consensus dispatch because the configured LAN gateway address belonged to the previous network interface. The later run used the existing gateway at the current interface address; no gateway restart.

An initial node-a identity timeout put that endpoint into cooldown. After node-b was deliberately made unavailable, the pool correctly used the already explicitly selected MEVBlocker endpoint. The old harness incorrectly required an unhealthy sibling. The final harness first verifies both siblings independently and adds the external fallback only at the later stage.
